paragraphs.text: Native DeepSeek Harness LaTeX workspace: edit .tex in the sidebar, compile with local TeX Live latex
mk, and keep a live PDF preview refreshed on save.
# dsh-latex

A native DeepSeek Harness
(`dsh`) plugin for the full local LaTeX loop: **open a `.tex` file in the

sidebar editor → save and compile with TeX Live `latexmk` → read structured
diagnostics → watch the
PDF preview refresh in place**.

It is a real DSH bundle with a Host half and a Web Client half, not a wrapper
script. Install it thr

ough DSH's plugin manager; no build step or npm
dependencies are required.
## Features

- **Edit `.tex` directly in the right sidebar.** Opening any `.tex` file address
claims it with an e

xtension-priority tab type, so DSH opens the plugin's
line-numbered editor instead of the read-only

document preview. Chapter files
resolve to their real main document on save.
- **Save = compile = re

fresh.** The triangle button (or Ctrl+S) runs immediately;
by default the editor also **auto-saves a

nd compiles after you stop typing**
(900 ms debounce, configurable). An open PDF preview updates thr

ough DSH's
SSE state stream; the first successful save opens one if none is open.
- **Structured dia

gnostics.** Failures show the error count and the first
`file:line` message in the editor; `latex_ge

t_diagnostics` and
`latex_get_status` return the full structured result to the agent.
- **Safe write

s.** Only existing `.tex` files, only inside the configured
`allowedRoots` fence, no UNC/network pat

hs, realpath re-validation, 4 MiB
cap, UTF-8 validation, BOM/EOL preservation, atomic replace and a

revision
compare-and-swap (external edits produce a conflict instead of being
overwritten).
- **PDF

preview.** PDF.js viewer with page jump, fit-width and 25–200% zoom,
lazy page rendering, stale-buil

d banner, last-good PDF preservation, and
double-click inverse SyncTeX (opens the editor at the corr

esponding line).
- **Agent tools.** Seven tools: compile, preview, diagnostics, status, clean,
cance

l, SyncTeX.
- **Project detection.** Explicit main file, `% !TEX root`, the file's own
`\documentcla

ss`, reverse `\input`/`\include` graph, and the session
workspace. Multi-root projects are separate

projects.
- **No shell, no default shell escape.** `latexmk` receives an argv array; a
project `.lat

exmkrc` is honoured by default and `allowProjectLatexmkrc: false`
passes `-norc`.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness with the Web Client plugin system. Tested against
**0.2.1-rc.5** on Windows 11. T

he POSIX code path is implemented but has not
been end-to-end tested.
- TeX Live (or another TeX dis

tribution) with `latexmk` and at least one of
`xelatex`, `pdflatex`, `lualatex`; optional `biber`, `

bibtex`, `synctex`.
- Node.js 20+ for the Host half (DSH ships its own Electron runtime; this is
onl

y about the plugin code).
- PDF.js is vendored in `assets/` (Apache-2.0); the plugin makes no networ

k
requests at runtime.

### From the marketplace

Once the plugin is listed in the DSH plugin catalog, search for **dsh-latex**
in **Plugins → Discove

r** (or the dsh-market plugin) and click Install. The
catalog entry points at the GitHub release tar

## How it works

- **Host** (`index.js`, `src/*.js`): project resolver, project registry, build
queue with a global s

emaphore, recursive source watcher with debounce and
auto-build coalescing, `latexmk` argv construct

ion, log/BibTeX/Biber parsing,
last-good PDF publication, SyncTeX, seven tools and the loopback HTTP

/SSE
surface.
- **Client** (`client.js`): a `.tex`-claiming resource tab (line-numbered
textarea edi

tor with save/compile/reload/preview controls), a PDF.js preview
tab, and compact tool-result cards.

No external JS dependencies; React is
provided by DSH's module table.
- **State**: build queue and

diagnostics are kept in the Host process; the last
successful preview version is persisted in
`<buil

dDir>/.dsh-latex/last-build-<fingerprint>.json` and restored after a
restart. Full build history is

not persisted.
- **HTTP surface** (same-origin, loopback): `GET /latex/health`, `/state`,
`/events`

(SSE), `/file?path=`, `/pdf?project=`, `/log?project=`,
`/assets/*`, `POST /file`, `POST /action` (i

ncluding `compile-file`),
`GET /synctex`, `POST /synctex-inverse`. Everything except `health` uses t

he
Harness connection admission; the PDF route serves only a registered
project's published preview.
`POST /file` is not a general filesystem API.
## Security

TeX compilation is **not a sandbox**: a project can execute code through
`.latexmkrc` and TeX's file

primitives, and the editor write API runs with Host
permissions. The full threat model and reportin

g process are in
SECURITY.md. In short:

is executable Perl and is honoured by default —
set `allowProjectLatexmkrc: false` for untrusted pro
a low-privilege container/VM.
## Limitations

- The editor is a plain `<textarea>` plus line numbers: no syntax highlighting,
autocomplete or mult

i-cursor. Auto-save is debounced and can be disabled with
`editorAutoSave: false`; the triangle butt

on and Ctrl+S always build
immediately.
- Closing an editor tab discards unsaved text; switching tab

s does not
(`keepMounted`).
- Only UTF-8 `.tex` files up to 4 MiB can be edited; new files and direc

tories
cannot be created from the editor.
- Build history and diagnostics live in Host memory; a res

tart restores the
last successful preview version but not historical diagnostics.
- PDF preview stat

e (page/zoom) is kept per project for the session; the
preview tab itself is one per session.
- The

browser half is tested on DSH 0.2.1-rc.5/Windows 11; other platforms and
older/newer DSH releases sh

ould be treated as untested.
- `.latexmkrc` and TeX file I/O are documented security boundaries, not

e treated as untested.
- `.latexmkrc` and TeX file I/O are documented security boundaries, not bugs.
More detail: docs/limitations.md.
